question: A 14-month-old African American boy is brought to the emergency department because of fever, lethargy, and lack of appetite for 6 days. The patient’s mother says he fell off the changing table 10 days ago and landed on his left side, which she says has been tender since then. His vital signs include: temperature 38.0°C (100.4°F), blood pressure 85/41 mm Hg, pulse 132/min. Physical examination reveals conjunctival pallor and reduced range of motion at the left hip. C-reactive protein (CRP) is raised. A magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan shows signs of infection in the medullary canal of the left femoral bone and surrounding soft tissues. Blood cultures are positive for Salmonella. Which of the following would most likely confirm the underlying diagnosis in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Fever, lethargy, lack of appetite" -> "Recent history of trauma to left side" -> "Tender left side" -> "Reduced range of motion at left hip" -> "Positive blood cultures for Salmonella" -> "Osteomyelitis due to Salmonella infection" -> "MRI showing signs of infection in left femoral bone" -> "Raised CRP" -> "Confirmatory test needed" -> 60%

enhanced_information: The most likely confirmatory test for the underlying diagnosis of osteomyelitis due to Salmonella infection in this patient would be a full blood count to assess for anemia or leukocytosis, given the clinical presentation and positive blood cultures for Salmonella.
analysis: The core medical principle in this case is to confirm the underlying diagnosis of osteomyelitis due to Salmonella infection. Given the clinical presentation of fever, lethargy, lack of appetite, tenderness at the left side, positive blood cultures for Salmonella, and MRI findings, the most likely correct option would be a full blood count to assess for anemia or leukocytosis, which are common findings in osteomyelitis. Anemia and leukocytosis are nonspecific markers of inflammation and infection, which would support the diagnosis in this patient.
